findings.path: scripts/e2e-android.js — warm-up cost and first-dump trade-off (non-blocking observation)
findings.problem: Two minor observations, neither blocking. (1) The warm-up dump adds up to 50s (45s dump timeout + 5s fallback sleep) before the Demarrer waitFor() window begins; the window extension (+60s) covers this with +10s net headroom even in the worst case, and in the success case the warm-up takes ~2-45s and makes subsequent real dumps fast, so the effective number of usable dump cycles within the window is higher than before. (2) If the warm-up dump itself hangs for the full 45s, that time is spent before the window rather than inside it — but the window extension more than compensates, and the warm-up is non-fatal (WARN + 5s sleep fallback), so a warm-up failure degrades to the previous behavior plus the window extension. The Auditor could not independently read the raw step-7 logs (no token in the audit environment); the repair is consistent with the public timing evidence and the documented flakiness chain.

Timing analysis: warm-up worst case 50s vs window extension 60s (net +10s); 360s window fits 4.8 failed-dump cycles (75s each) vs 4.0 with 300s.
